kpis.name: Retail units sold
kpis.purpose: The primary volume measure of the business, and the denominator of every per-unit gross measure. It answers how many cars the group delivered.
kpis.definition: The count of finalized retail and lease deliveries in the period. Wholesale disposals and dealer trades are not retail units and are never counted here.
kpis.formula: SUM(unit_count) WHERE is_retail = true
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) over rows where is_retail = true, restricted to the selected period and filter context.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Integer count. Thousands separator. No decimals.
kpis.grain: Store x day; fully additive across store, day, employee, vehicle, model, and lead source; aggregates to any period without restatement.
kpis.dateBasis: warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.sale_date_key to warehouse.dim_date. Sale date, not delivery date; delivery-date reporting via delivery_date_key must be labelled as such.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. An empty filter context returns 0, never BLANK(), because no cars sold is a meaningful business answer that must be visible on a trend line.
kpis.caution: Volume alone must never be used to rank employees or stores; a high-volume employee may show weak gross retention, poor follow-up, or heavy discounting. Always pair with KPI-GRS-006 and funnel context.

kpis.name: New units sold
kpis.purpose: Isolates new-vehicle volume, which behaves differently from used in supply constraint, gross structure, and incentive exposure; required for the new-versus-used comparison.
kpis.definition: The count of finalized retail and lease deliveries of new vehicles in the period.
kpis.formula: SUM(unit_count) WHERE is_retail = true AND the vehicle's condition is New
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) over rows where is_retail = true and warehouse.dim_vehicle.condition_type = 'New'. Exposed as reporting.vw_vehicle_sales.new_unit_count.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Integer count. Thousands separator.
kpis.grain: Store x day; fully additive.
kpis.dateBasis: sale_date_key to dim_date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. Returns 0 in an empty context. Structurally 0 for GSA-003, an independent used store with no franchise; that zero is correct, not missing data.
kpis.caution: New-vehicle gross is affected by manufacturer incentives, which are excluded from the initial model, so new-unit profitability in ARPI is incomplete by design; comparisons to used gross must say so.

kpis.name: Used units sold
kpis.purpose: Isolates used-vehicle volume, where acquisition skill, reconditioning discipline, and pricing judgement show up, and where gross variance is widest.
kpis.definition: The count of finalized retail and lease deliveries of used vehicles, including manufacturer-certified pre-owned units, in the period.
kpis.formula: SUM(unit_count) WHERE is_retail = true AND the vehicle's condition is Used or Certified
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) over rows where is_retail = true and warehouse.dim_vehicle.condition_type IN ('Used', 'Certified'). Exposed as reporting.vw_vehicle_sales.used_unit_count.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Integer count. Thousands separator.
kpis.grain: Store x day; fully additive.
kpis.dateBasis: sale_date_key to dim_date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. Returns 0 in an empty context.
kpis.caution: Certified units are included here by definition; any report separating used and certified must state whether used is inclusive or exclusive of certified, since both conventions exist and mixing them double-counts or under-counts.

kpis.name: Front-end gross
kpis.purpose: Profit earned on the vehicle itself; the measure most sensitive to pricing, discounting, acquisition cost, and reconditioning discipline.
kpis.definition: Total vehicle profit on finalized retail deliveries: selling price less what the unit cost to acquire, recondition, and pack.
kpis.formula: SUM(final sale price - acquisition cost - reconditioning cost - pack amount)
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.front_end_gross) over rows where is_retail = true; front_end_gross = sale_price - acquisition_cost - reconditioning_cost - pack_amount, computed in SQL at load.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Currency, USD, no decimals at summary level.
kpis.grain: Store x day; fully additive.
kpis.dateBasis: sale_date_key to dim_date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. Returns 0 in an empty context. Negative values are legitimate and must remain visible; a negative-front deal is a real dealership outcome.
kpis.caution: Because incentives are excluded, new-vehicle front gross is systematically understated relative to a real store; this is a modelling boundary, not a finding, and must never be implied to reflect real-world profitability.

kpis.name: Back-end gross
kpis.purpose: Profit earned in the finance office; shows whether total profitability is carried by the vehicle or by F&I, a central management question.
kpis.definition: The sum of net finance reserve and net F&I product gross on finalized retail deliveries.
kpis.formula: SUM(net finance reserve + net F&I product gross)
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.back_end_gross) over rows where is_retail = true; generated directly at deal level in the MVP, becoming a derived total once warehouse.fact_finance_product_sale exists.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Currency, USD, no decimals at summary level.
kpis.grain: Store x day; fully additive.
kpis.dateBasis: sale_date_key to dim_date. Cancellations/chargebacks occur after the sale, so restatement is expected once the deferred F&I fact exists; until then, back-end gross is as-booked.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. Returns 0 in an empty context. A cash deal with no products legitimately contributes 0, not NULL.
kpis.caution: In the MVP, back-end gross is a single generated number with no product-level detail; it cannot answer which product drove it, and any narrative about product mix is unsupported until the deferred F&I fact is built.

kpis.name: Total gross
kpis.purpose: The headline profitability figure and the single most-quoted number in dealership management reporting.
kpis.definition: Front-end gross plus back-end gross on finalized retail deliveries.
kpis.formula: front-end gross + back-end gross
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.total_gross) over rows where is_retail = true, where total_gross = front_end_gross + back_end_gross, stored at load rather than recomputed at query time.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Currency, USD, no decimals at summary level.
kpis.grain: Store x day; fully additive.
kpis.dateBasis: sale_date_key to dim_date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. Returns 0 in an empty context. May be negative; must remain visible.
kpis.caution: Total gross conceals the trade-off between front and back; a flat total gross trend can hide a collapsing front offset by rising F&I, a materially different business. Always show KPI-GRS-001 and KPI-GRS-002 alongside it.

kpis.name: Front gross per retail unit
kpis.purpose: Normalizes vehicle profit for volume so stores of different sizes can be compared, and so a profit change can be attributed to pricing rather than volume.
kpis.definition: Average vehicle profit earned on each retail unit delivered in the period.
kpis.formula: total retail front-end gross / retail units sold
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.front_end_gross) over rows where is_retail = true, in the filter context.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) over rows where is_retail = true, same filter context; must exclude wholesale and dealer-trade transactions.
kpis.unit: Currency per unit, USD, no decimals, e.g. $1,842.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive; must be recomputed at every level of aggregation, never summed or averaged from lower levels.
kpis.dateBasis: sale_date_key to dim_date. Numerator and denominator must use the identical date basis and filter context.
kpis.nullBehaviour: When the denominator is 0, returns BLANK()/NULL, never 0; zero units sold means the metric is undefined. Charts must show a gap, not a zero point.
kpis.caution: A rising per-unit gross with falling volume is not automatically good; it may mean the store stopped chasing marginal deals. Pair with KPI-SLS-001. Never compare to an external benchmark.

kpis.name: Back gross per retail unit
kpis.purpose: The standard measure of finance-office productivity; answers how much is earned in F&I on every car delivered.
kpis.definition: Average finance and insurance profit earned on each retail unit delivered in the period.
kpis.formula: total retail back-end gross / retail units sold
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.back_end_gross) over rows where is_retail = true.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) over rows where is_retail = true, same filter context; wholesale and dealer trades excluded.
kpis.unit: Currency per unit, USD, no decimals.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: sale_date_key to dim_date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero denominator returns BLANK()/NULL. A cash deal with no F&I products contributes 0 to the numerator and 1 to the denominator; it is included so cash deals do not overstate finance-office productivity.
kpis.caution: The denominator includes cash deals, which cannot generate finance reserve; a store with an unusual cash mix will show a lower figure for reasons unrelated to finance-office skill. Cross-store comparisons must control for deal-type mix.

kpis.name: Total gross per retail unit
kpis.purpose: The single most useful summary of deal quality, and the correct companion to unit volume in any employee or store comparison.
kpis.definition: Average total profit, vehicle plus finance office, earned on each retail unit delivered in the period.
kpis.formula: total retail gross / retail units sold
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.total_gross) over rows where is_retail = true.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) over rows where is_retail = true, same filter context; must exclude wholesale and dealer-trade transactions.
kpis.unit: Currency per unit, USD, no decimals.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: sale_date_key to dim_date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero denominator returns BLANK()/NULL.
kpis.caution: The correct counterweight to volume in employee analysis, but not sufficient alone; scorecards must carry contextual metrics such as lead volume, source mix, tenure, and inventory availability, since ranking on gross per unit alone penalizes whoever gets the harder inventory.

kpis.name: Active inventory count
kpis.purpose: How many units the group is carrying; the base of every inventory-health measure and the numerator of days supply.
kpis.definition: The number of vehicles physically in stock at a store on a given snapshot date.
kpis.formula: SUM(inventory_unit_count)
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot.inventory_unit_count) for rows whose snapshot_date_key equals the single selected as-of date.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Integer count. Thousands separator.
kpis.grain: Store x snapshot date. Semi-additive across store, vehicle, model, not across dates; summing over a month yields unit-days, not units.
kpis.dateBasis: snapshot_date_key to dim_date. A single as-of date, defaulting to the latest snapshot in the model.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. Returns 0 when no units are in stock. Returns BLANK() if the selected date has no snapshot rows at all, signalling missing data rather than an empty lot.
kpis.caution: Semi-additivity is the most common way this measure is misreported; a month-level card showing a summed daily count is wrong by roughly a factor of 30 and looks plausible. Every visual must state its time-aggregation rule.

kpis.name: Inventory investment
kpis.purpose: How much capital is tied up in stock; converts an aging problem from a count into a dollar figure, making it a management priority.
kpis.definition: The total money invested in the vehicles in stock on a given date: acquisition cost plus reconditioning spend.
kpis.formula: SUM(acquisition_cost + reconditioning_cost)
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot.inventory_investment) for rows on the selected as-of date, where inventory_investment = acquisition_cost + reconditioning_cost.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Currency, USD, no decimals; large values may be abbreviated, tooltip shows full figure.
kpis.grain: Store x snapshot date. Semi-additive, same rule as KPI-INV-001.
kpis.dateBasis: snapshot_date_key to dim_date, single as-of date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. Returns 0 when no units are in stock; BLANK() when the date has no snapshot rows.
kpis.caution: This is cost invested, not market value or floor-plan exposure. ARPI models no floor-plan interest, holding cost, or carrying cost, so statements about what aged inventory costs per day are not supportable from this data.

kpis.name: Average inventory age
kpis.purpose: Mean days in stock across the active lot; retained for reconciliation and, against the median, as a direct indicator of an aged tail. Not the headline age figure.
kpis.definition: The arithmetic mean number of days that the vehicles currently in stock have been in stock.
kpis.formula: SUM(days_in_stock) / COUNT(active units)
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot.days_in_stock) for rows on the selected snapshot date, where days_in_stock is calendar days between acquisition date and snapshot date.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot.inventory_unit_count) for the same snapshot date and filter context, i.e. KPI-INV-001.
kpis.unit: Days, one decimal place.
kpis.grain: Store x snapshot date. Non-additive ratio; also semi-additive in its denominator. Must be recomputed at every aggregation level and date.
kpis.dateBasis: snapshot_date_key to dim_date, single as-of date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero denominator returns BLANK()/NULL. An empty lot has no average age; it does not have an average age of zero.
kpis.caution: The mean is the wrong headline for this right-skewed distribution; a small number of very old units pulls it well above the typical unit. Use KPI-INV-004 as the headline and read the mean-minus-median gap as evidence of an aged tail.

kpis.name: Median inventory age
kpis.purpose: The headline inventory-age figure; describes the typical unit on the lot without distortion from the aged tail.
kpis.definition: The middle value of days-in-stock across the vehicles currently in stock: half the lot is younger, half is older.
kpis.formula: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_in_stock)
kpis.numerator: n/a - order statistic; the input population is warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot.days_in_stock for all rows on the selected snapshot date in the filter context.
kpis.denominator: n/a - order statistic
kpis.unit: Days, integer.
kpis.grain: Store x snapshot date. Not additive or decomposable; group median is not derivable from subgroup medians and must be recomputed from rows.
kpis.dateBasis: snapshot_date_key to dim_date, single as-of date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Returns BLANK()/NULL when the population is empty. With an even population size, the linear-interpolated median (PERCENTILE_CONT) is used and rounded to the nearest whole day for display.
kpis.caution: Deliberately insensitive to the aged tail, making it the right typical-unit figure and the wrong risk figure; read alongside KPI-INV-005 and KPI-INV-006. Neither may be compared to an industry standard, because ARPI has none.

kpis.name: Aged inventory count
kpis.purpose: The number of units that have crossed the aging threshold; the actionable list of units requiring a pricing or disposal decision.
kpis.definition: The count of vehicles in stock on the selected date whose days-in-stock exceeds the selected age threshold.
kpis.formula: SUM(inventory_unit_count) WHERE days_in_stock > age_threshold
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot.inventory_unit_count) for rows on the selected snapshot date where days_in_stock > @age_threshold.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Integer count.
kpis.grain: Store x snapshot date. Semi-additive across dates, exactly like KPI-INV-001.
kpis.dateBasis: snapshot_date_key to dim_date, single as-of date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. Returns 0 when no units exceed the threshold, a genuine and good business answer.
kpis.caution: The threshold (defaulting to 60 days, a project default, not an industry benchmark) is a convention; different operators use 30, 45, 60, or 90 days. Any finding depending on the threshold must state it in the same sentence.

kpis.name: Aged inventory percentage
kpis.purpose: Normalizes aged-unit exposure for lot size so stores with different inventory volumes can be compared on one scale; the standard inventory-health indicator on an executive page.
kpis.definition: The share of the active lot that has been in stock longer than the selected age threshold.
kpis.formula: active inventory units above selected age threshold / total active inventory units
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot.inventory_unit_count) on the selected snapshot date where days_in_stock > @age_threshold, i.e. KPI-INV-005.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot.inventory_unit_count) on the same snapshot date and filter context, with no age filter, i.e. KPI-INV-001.
kpis.unit: Percentage, one decimal place, e.g. 18.4%.
kpis.grain: Store x snapshot date. Non-additive ratio; recompute at every level.
kpis.dateBasis: snapshot_date_key to dim_date, single as-of date, identical on both sides.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero denominator returns BLANK()/NULL. Numerator 0 with a non-zero denominator correctly returns 0.0%.
kpis.caution: Can improve for a bad reason: wholesaling aged units removes them from the numerator, so the percentage falls while the group takes a loss. Read alongside KPI-INV-002 and wholesale volume; ARPI has no benchmark for a healthy aged percentage.

kpis.name: Days to sale
kpis.purpose: How long it actually took to sell the units that sold; the outcome measure that pairs with inventory age's in-flight measure.
kpis.definition: The number of calendar days between acquiring a vehicle and finalizing its sale, published as median (headline) and mean (companion).
kpis.formula: Per unit: finalized sale date - acquisition date. Aggregate median: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_in_inventory_at_sale). Aggregate mean: SUM(days_in_inventory_at_sale) / SUM(unit_count).
kpis.numerator: For the mean: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.days_in_inventory_at_sale) over rows where is_retail = true. For the median: n/a - order statistic over the same population.
kpis.denominator: For the mean: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) over rows where is_retail = true, same filter context. For the median: n/a - order statistic.
kpis.unit: Days; median as integer, mean to one decimal; both labelled explicitly.
kpis.grain: One value per sale transaction; aggregable to store x period as median or mean. Neither aggregate is additive.
kpis.dateBasis: sale_date_key to dim_date. Units are attributed to the period they sold, not acquired.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Both aggregates return BLANK()/NULL when no retail units sold in context. days_in_inventory_at_sale is non-negative by rule; sale date cannot precede acquisition date.
kpis.caution: Survivorship bias is dominant: this measure describes only units that sold, so a lot full of 300-day units that never sell can show an excellent figure. Always read with KPI-INV-004 and KPI-INV-006; retail only, new and used reported separately.

kpis.name: Inventory turn
kpis.purpose: How many times the lot is sold and replaced in a year; the standard efficiency measure for working capital deployed in inventory.
kpis.definition: Annualized retail sales volume divided by the average number of retail units held in stock over the same period.
kpis.formula: annualized retail units sold / average active retail inventory
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) where is_retail = true over the period, annualized as x (365 / number_of_calendar_days_in_the_selected_period), using calendar days not selling days.
kpis.denominator: AVG(daily active inventory count): SUM(inventory_unit_count) / COUNT(DISTINCT snapshot_date_key) from warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot, same filter context; a true daily average.
kpis.unit: Turns per year, two decimals, e.g. 8.42; annualization stated on the visual.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: Numerator: sale_date_key. Denominator: snapshot_date_key. Two different date columns over the same period window, both driven by the same period selection.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero denominator returns BLANK()/NULL. A period with no snapshot rows returns BLANK(), not 0.
kpis.caution: Turn and days-supply calculations vary across vendors; ARPI's method (calendar-day annualization, retail-only numerator, daily-average denominator, new/used separated) is not comparable to another system unless it uses the same choices. Unstable over short windows; minimum window one month.

kpis.name: Dealer days supply
kpis.purpose: How long the current lot would last at the recent selling pace; the operational counterpart to turn, used to decide whether to buy more inventory.
kpis.definition: The number of days the current inventory would cover, given average daily retail sales over the recent trailing window.
kpis.formula: current active inventory / average daily retail sales over the selected trailing period
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_inventory_snapshot.inventory_unit_count) on the single as-of date (the latest snapshot date in context), i.e. KPI-INV-001.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) where is_retail = true over the trailing @trailing_days calendar days ending on the as-of date, divided by @trailing_days.
kpis.unit: Days, integer; the trailing window must be stated on the visual.
kpis.grain: Store x as-of date. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: Numerator: snapshot_date_key = as-of date. Denominator: sale_date_key in [as_of_date - @trailing_days + 1, as_of_date].
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero sales in the trailing window returns BLANK()/NULL, never infinity or a sentinel number; the visual must show insufficient sales history rather than a value.
kpis.caution: Extremely sensitive to the trailing window (default 30 calendar days, a project default not a benchmark) and to seasonality; a slow-month window makes a normal lot look overstocked. ARPI publishes no target days supply.

kpis.name: Leads received
kpis.purpose: Top-of-funnel volume; the denominator of contact rate and lead-to-sale conversion, and the basis of marketing cost per lead.
kpis.definition: The count of valid, non-duplicate CRM leads created in the period.
kpis.formula: SUM(lead_count) WHERE is_duplicate = false
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_lead.lead_count) over rows where is_duplicate = false.
kpis.denominator: n/a - additive measure
kpis.unit: Integer count. Thousands separator.
kpis.grain: Store x day; fully additive.
kpis.dateBasis: lead_created_date_key to dim_date. Leads count in the period created, regardless of when or whether they later converted.
kpis.nullBehaviour: No denominator. Returns 0 in an empty context.
kpis.caution: Vendor-reported lead counts will not match this measure, and are not expected to, since vendors count differently and typically include duplicates; that discrepancy is an analytical finding to report, not a defect to hide.

kpis.name: Contact rate
kpis.purpose: The first funnel stage, and the one most directly under BDC control; a weak contact rate makes every downstream rate irrelevant.
kpis.definition: The share of valid leads with which the store established two-way contact.
kpis.formula: unique contacted leads / valid nonduplicate leads
kpis.numerator: COUNT(DISTINCT warehouse.fact_lead.lead_key) where is_contacted = true and is_duplicate = false.
kpis.denominator: COUNT(DISTINCT warehouse.fact_lead.lead_key) where is_duplicate = false, i.e. KPI-FUN-001, same filter context.
kpis.unit: Percentage, one decimal place.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: lead_created_date_key to dim_date on both sides, anchored to lead creation not contact date, so late-period leads are not counted before they had a fair chance to be contacted.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero denominator returns BLANK()/NULL. Zero contacted with a non-zero denominator correctly returns 0.0%.
kpis.caution: Right-censoring: leads created near period end may not yet be contacted, depressing the rate. Period-to-date comparisons need the same maturity window applied to both periods; also not comparable across sources without controlling for source.

kpis.name: Appointment-set rate
kpis.purpose: Measures whether contact is being converted into a scheduled visit, the step that most strongly predicts a sale.
kpis.definition: Of the leads the store actually reached, the share for which an appointment was booked.
kpis.formula: unique leads with an appointment set / unique contacted leads
kpis.numerator: COUNT(DISTINCT warehouse.fact_lead.lead_key) where is_appointment_set = true and is_duplicate = false.
kpis.denominator: COUNT(DISTINCT warehouse.fact_lead.lead_key) where is_contacted = true and is_duplicate = false, i.e. the numerator of KPI-FUN-002, same filter context.
kpis.unit: Percentage, one decimal place.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: lead_created_date_key to dim_date on both sides.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero contacted leads returns BLANK()/NULL.
kpis.caution: Because the denominator is conditional on contact, this rate cannot be read without KPI-FUN-002 alongside it; a store reaching 20% of leads could otherwise look better than one reaching 70%.

kpis.name: Show rate
kpis.purpose: Whether booked appointments actually turn into people in the showroom; distinguishes appointment-setting activity from appointment-setting quality.
kpis.definition: The share of appointments eligible to show at which the customer actually arrived.
kpis.formula: appointments that showed / scheduled appointments eligible to show
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_appointment.appointment_count) where is_shown = true.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_appointment.appointment_count) where is_cancelled_in_advance = false and scheduled date is on or before period end. Exposed as reporting.vw_appointments.eligible_appointment_count.
kpis.unit: Percentage, one decimal place.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive ratio, computed over appointments rather than leads; one lead can produce several appointments.
kpis.dateBasis: scheduled_date_key to dim_date on both sides, not the created date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero eligible appointments returns BLANK()/NULL.
kpis.caution: The cancellation exclusion is the manipulable part of this measure; a store that marks no-shows as advance cancellations reports a flattering show rate, so cancellation rate must be published on the same visual.

kpis.name: Show-to-sale conversion
kpis.purpose: The closing rate on customers who physically arrived; isolates showroom and salesperson performance from BDC and marketing performance.
kpis.definition: Of the appointments where the customer showed up, the share that resulted in a finalized retail sale.
kpis.formula: shown appointments linked to a finalized retail sale / shown appointments
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_appointment.appointment_count) where is_shown/is_sold = true and sale_key resolves to a finalized sale. Exposed as reporting.vw_appointments.shown_and_sold_appointment_count.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_appointment.appointment_count) where is_shown = true, same filter context.
kpis.unit: Percentage, one decimal place.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive ratio, computed over appointments.
kpis.dateBasis: show_date_key to dim_date on both sides, attributing to the visit date rather than the sale date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero shown appointments returns BLANK()/NULL.
kpis.caution: A customer who visits at month end and buys days later is attributed to the visit date, so late-period conversion appears to improve as data matures; period-to-date figures must be labelled incomplete. Walk-in traffic without an appointment is not included at all.

kpis.name: Lead-to-sale conversion
kpis.purpose: The end-to-end funnel result; the measure that determines whether a lead source is worth paying for.
kpis.definition: The share of valid leads that ultimately resulted in a finalized retail sale.
kpis.formula: unique leads linked to a finalized retail sale / valid nonduplicate leads
kpis.numerator: COUNT(DISTINCT warehouse.fact_lead.lead_key) where is_sold = true, is_duplicate = false, and sale_key resolves to a finalized retail sale. Exposed as reporting.vw_leads.sold_lead_count.
kpis.denominator: COUNT(DISTINCT warehouse.fact_lead.lead_key) where is_duplicate = false, i.e. KPI-FUN-001, same filter context.
kpis.unit: Percentage, one decimal place.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: lead_created_date_key to dim_date on both sides; a lead created in March that sells in May counts in March, the lead's cohort rather than the sale's period.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero valid leads returns BLANK()/NULL.
kpis.caution: Cohort maturity dominates: recent months always look worst since those leads have not finished converting. Attribution is single-source, first-touch; multi-touch attribution is out of scope.

kpis.name: Average response time
kpis.purpose: Mean time to first response; retained as the companion to the median and for total-response-seconds reconciliation. Not the headline responsiveness figure.
kpis.definition: The arithmetic mean number of minutes between a lead arriving and the store's first outbound response.
kpis.formula: SUM(first_response_seconds) / COUNT(leads with a response) / 60
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_lead.first_response_seconds) over rows where first_response_seconds IS NOT NULL and is_duplicate = false, divided by 60 for display in minutes.
kpis.denominator: COUNT(warehouse.fact_lead.lead_key) where first_response_seconds IS NOT NULL and is_duplicate = false, same filter context.
kpis.unit: Minutes, one decimal place; values over 24 hours shown in hours with the unit stated.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: lead_created_date_key to dim_date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero responded leads returns BLANK()/NULL. first_response_seconds = 0 (instant auto-response) is valid and included; only NULL is excluded.
kpis.caution: Two compounding distortions: the distribution is severely right-skewed so one late lead can move a store-month's mean, and excluding never-responded leads makes the worst outcomes invisible. Use the median as the headline.

kpis.name: Median response time
kpis.purpose: The headline responsiveness figure; describes what the typical customer actually experiences, undistorted by the tail.
kpis.definition: The middle value of first-response times: half of responded leads were answered faster, half slower.
kpis.formula: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY first_response_seconds) / 60
kpis.numerator: n/a - order statistic; the input population is warehouse.fact_lead.first_response_seconds for rows where the value is not NULL and is_duplicate = false.
kpis.denominator: n/a - order statistic
kpis.unit: Minutes, integer.
kpis.grain: Store x period. Not additive and not decomposable; must be recomputed from row-level values at every aggregation level.
kpis.dateBasis: lead_created_date_key to dim_date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Returns BLANK()/NULL when the population is empty. Even-sized populations use linear-interpolated PERCENTILE_CONT, fixed so SQL and DAX agree.
kpis.caution: Shares the never-responded exclusion with KPI-FUN-007 and is equally blind to ignored leads; must be published with the count of leads without follow-up. ARPI states no target response time, having no benchmark data.

kpis.name: Marketing cost per lead
kpis.purpose: What the store pays to generate one opportunity; the first-order efficiency measure for a paid channel.
kpis.definition: Marketing spend divided by the number of valid leads attributed to that source or campaign in the same month.
kpis.formula: marketing spend / valid leads attributed to the source or campaign
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_marketing_spend.spend_amount) for the selected store, campaign, and month.
kpis.denominator: COUNT(DISTINCT warehouse.fact_lead.lead_key) where is_duplicate = false, attributed to the same campaign_key (or lead_source_key), lead_created_date_key in the same month as the spend row.
kpis.unit: Currency per lead, USD, two decimals.
kpis.grain: Store x campaign x month. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: Spend: month_date_key to dim_date. Leads: lead_created_date_key to dim_date, aggregated to the same month.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero leads with non-zero spend returns BLANK()/NULL, not infinity; the visual must surface that case explicitly. Zero spend with leads present returns 0.
kpis.caution: Grain mismatch is the central caution: spend is monthly while leads are daily, so this measure must never be computed at day grain. Attribution is single-source, first-touch, and cost per lead says nothing about lead quality.

kpis.name: Marketing cost per sale
kpis.purpose: What the store pays to generate one delivered car; corrects for lead quality, which cost per lead ignores entirely.
kpis.definition: Marketing spend divided by the number of finalized retail sales attributed to that source or campaign.
kpis.formula: marketing spend / finalized retail sales attributed to the source or campaign
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_marketing_spend.spend_amount) for the selected store, campaign, and month.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.unit_count) where is_retail = true, originating lead attributed to the same campaign_key (or lead_source_key), lead's creation month equal to the spend month.
kpis.unit: Currency per sale, USD, no decimals.
kpis.grain: Store x campaign x month. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: Spend: month_date_key. Sales: attributed via the originating lead's lead_created_date_key, not the sale date.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero attributed sales with non-zero spend returns BLANK()/NULL, not infinity; reported as spend with no attributed sales.
kpis.caution: Cohort immaturity is severe: leads created this month have not finished converting, so current-month cost per sale always looks worst and improves for weeks afterward. Attribution remains single-source, first-touch.

kpis.name: Gross return on advertising spend
kpis.purpose: Whether a channel makes money after the cost of the cars it sells; the only marketing return measure ARPI treats as primary.
kpis.definition: Total gross profit attributed to a source or campaign, divided by the marketing spend on it. A value of 1.0 means the channel returned exactly its cost in gross profit.
kpis.formula: attributed total gross / marketing spend
kpis.numerator: SUM(warehouse.fact_vehicle_sale.total_gross) where is_retail = true and the originating lead is attributed to the campaign or source, with the lead's creation month equal to the spend month.
kpis.denominator: SUM(warehouse.fact_marketing_spend.spend_amount) for the same store, campaign, and month.
kpis.unit: Ratio, two decimals, e.g. 3.42; may be shown as a multiple (3.4x), not as a percentage.
kpis.grain: Store x campaign x month. Non-additive ratio.
kpis.dateBasis: Both sides anchored to the spend month; sales attributed via the originating lead's creation month.
kpis.nullBehaviour: Zero spend returns BLANK()/NULL, never infinity; gross with zero spend is an organic result, not an infinite return.
kpis.caution: Revenue return must not be presented as the primary profitability measure; ARPI publishes gross-based return as primary. This does not net out personnel, facility, or floor-plan cost, so it is a contribution measure, not a profit measure. No target value is published.
